articles.title: Marcos wants remaining POGOs, illegal contraband gone
articles.summary: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. wants an end to Philippine Offshore Gaming Operators (POGOs) and other illegal activities within the country"s territory, according to the Palace on Tuesday.

blocks.text: Published October 20, 2026 4:14pm
President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. wants an end to Philippine Offshore Gaming Operators (POGOs) and other illegal activities within the country’s territory, according to the Palace on Tuesday.

Presidential Anti-Organized Crime Commission (PAOCC) spokesperson Winston Casio recently stated that some POGO operations have continued despite Marcos banning the practice in 2024. Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said that if POGOs are still operating, then the PAOCC and the Philippine National Police Criminal Investigation and Detection Group will continue to act on it.

“Ang utos ng Pangulo patungkol dito sugpuin ang kontrabando. Kung anuman ang ilegal na ginagawa sa teritoryo ng Pilipinas dapat itong hanapin, papanagutin at huwag titigil hangga’t hindi nauubos ang mga activities na ginagawa ng mga gumagawa ng ganitong klaseng krimen,” Castro said in a media briefing.

(The President ordered that this contraband should stop. Whatever illegal activities are being done within the Philippines should be found out, held to account, and there is no stopping until these activities being done by perpetrators have all gone.)
Castro said that police have already raided several illegal POGO hubs, citing separate operations on October 2 in Zamboanga Sibugay, and another one last October 18 in Makati City.
Asked about Casio’s suggestion to review the visa-free arrangement for Chinese nationals, the Palace official said the matter has been raised to the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA).
“So, titingnan din po nila kung ano ang nagiging issue or nagkakaroon ba ito nang hindi magandang epekto,” Castro said.
(So, they will see what the issue is or if it has had some bad effects.)

Prior to its banning in 2024, POGOs have been linked to various illegal activities within the country by foreign nationals, with many of them being Chinese citizens. These crimes include human trafficking and the trade of illicit drugs. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Video of people panic-buying water drums for Super El Niño is AI-generated
articles.summary: Multiple satirical videos surfaced online after Marcos advised people to buy buckets to store water amid concerns over Super El Niño

blocks.text: Claim: Hordes of people are panic-buying water drums at a local warehouse after President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. advised the public to store water in preparation for the anticipated Super El Niño.
Why we fact-checked this: Facebook user Bonz Gimenez posted a viral video showing hundreds of people supposedly storming a water drum warehouse to hoard multiple containers.
The caption read, “Panic buying ng mga malalaking drums sa isang warehouse (Panic buying of large drums at a warehouse).”

The individuals in the video appeared hysterical, arguing over the plastic drums and pushing each other. Vehicles are scattered around the supposed warehouse, where people are shown loading the containers.
The video has garnered 20 million views, 257,000 reactions, 10,400 comments, and 26,000 shares as of writing.

While multiple commenters believe the video to be AI-generated, many still believe the claim. One Facebook user commented, “Hala? Ante Claire [Castro] at BBM (Marcos), nag-panic buying na ng mga drum at timba; ang galing niyo talaga!”
(Oh my? Auntie Claire and BBM, people have started panic-buying drums and pails — you guys are truly something else!)
Multiple users have also reposted the video, claiming it was the result of the President’s advice to the public to buy buckets to collect rainwater in preparation for the effects of Super El Niño.

The facts: The video is AI-generated. SightEngine, an AI detection tool, flagged screenshots of the video as 99% likely to be AI-generated. It also gave the video a score of 32%, with some frames reaching 66% and 99%. Similarly, Hive Detect also marked multiple parts of the video as 81% AI-generated.
There are also no reports from credible sources confirming the incident shown in the video.
The video and other satirical content about plastic water buckets were fueled by the President’s statement during an interview in Singapore on October 11.

While talking about the government’s plans to prepare for the anticipated water supply issue with the looming Super El Niño, Marcos said, “Bumili na kayo ng balde para ‘pag umulan, makolekta na ninyo lahat.”
(Buy buckets so when it rains, you can collect rainwater).
He added that the government would roll out an information campaign on filtering and storing rainwater, saying, “We’ll give you the filter; we’ll teach you how to do everything.”

Marcos’ bucket remark has drawn mixed reactions, but Palace Press Officer Claire Castro clapped back at government detractors in an October 13 statement, saying: “Hindi po ito pagkaniya-kaniya. Kung ito lang po ang narinig na patungkol sa balde, ang mas maganda po, umupo sila at makinig. Sit down and listen kung ano ang sinasabi ng Pangulo.”

(This is not about everyone fending for themselves. If all they heard was the remark about buckets, it would be better if they sat down and listened. Sit down and listen to what the President is saying.)
She added that Marcos’ advice was not a joke and should be taken seriously.
Meanwhile, Vice President Sara Duterte said on October 12 that she does not want to comment about Marcos’ bucket statement, but mentioned that “we can’t rely on the President.”

Water filtration: In an October 14 Palace briefing, the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) said it would distribute water filtration kits to communities vulnerable to El Niño, then demonstrated how to use them.

The DSWD will first distribute the kits to local government units that have declared a state of calamity due to El Niño, as well as high-density areas in Metro Manila experiencing low water pressure. (READ: DENR: 1 in 3 barangays nationwide highly vulnerable to El Niño)
Since 2024, the department has already deployed buckets with built-in water filtration technology to disaster-hit areas without access to potable water.
Higher demand: Markets are already seeing a high demand for buckets and water drums. Stores in Divisoria have begun procuring more supplies as people buy more than usual.

Vendors have assured the public that supplies remain available, even as one seller urged consumers to avoid panic buying. The government has also echoed this, as police continue to monitor the situation.

According to the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration, the current El Niño is expected to intensify into a very strong El Niño between the September–December 2026 season and persist through the first half of 2027. – Eirene Manatlao/Rappler.com

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.title: A contractor left this Toronto man without a roof. His insurance company is denying his claim
articles.summary: What began as a simple knock on the front door last spring has resulted in an elderly Scarborough man living out of a suitcase, his home roofless and in ruins. While police are investigating a…

image.caption: Lawrence Huang says he has been living in motels since contractors walked off the job after removing his roof. He says he has no way to pay for the rebuild, as his insurance company has denied his claim. (Michael Smee/CBC)

blocks.text: What began as a simple knock on the front door last spring has resulted in an elderly Scarborough man living out of a suitcase, his home roofless and in ruins.
Police are now investigating a possible fraud, while the man's home insurance company has denied most of his claim.

Lawrence Huang was approached in late May by representatives of a company called Super Dry Roofing and Masonry, who told him his roof was infested with rodents, seriously damaged, and in need of replacement.
The 76-year-old, whom his niece Katie Semple describes as “on the spectrum,” signed a roof replacement contract and gave a salesman for the company a $25,000 advance on the $50,000 job.
The contractor went to work, completely removing the roof of Huang’s two-storey Guildwood Parkway home, leaving the contents open to the elements.

The kitchen of Lawrence Huang's home, four months after contractors left the job site, with the home's roof removed. TD Insurance has said it will cover the cost of the home's ruined contents, but not the structural damage. (Mike Smee/CBC)

And the price began to rise. Semple says her uncle then handed over $1,800. Within weeks he gave the contractor another cheque, this time for $64,000 — at which point employees at his bank became suspicious, and refused to honour the large cheque. They also contacted police, the city and Semple, his only surviving relative.
Within days, the workers abruptly abandoned the site, leaving his home with no roof and a massive pile of scrap lumber in the driveway.
Semple says she has tried to contact Super Dry, but the phone number appears to be disconnected.
CBC Toronto has also attempted to contact the company using phone and email contacts listed on the contract. The phone number is not assigned and an email was returned as undeliverable.
Insurance won't cover 'faulty ... workmanship'

After Super Dry left, Huang initially tried living in the basement, but city engineers and Toronto Fire Service ordered him to leave. Since then, Semple says, he has been living in motels and trying to figure out how his home can be rebuilt — and how it will all be paid for.
The contents of his home, including valuable books and family mementoes, are now a sodden mess, destroyed by trespassers, rain and animals.
“It’s a lifetime of memories,” Semple said. “It’s terrible. I lost sleep. I don’t know what to do. I’m the only one he has left.”
Katie Semple stands in what was once the living room of her uncle's Scarborough home. She says trespassers have done damage, as has the weather. (Mike Smee/CBC)
Semple says her uncle’s insurer, TD Insurance, is refusing to cover most of the damage, including Huang’s rebuild, which he cannot afford to do on his own.

In a Sept. 9 letter to Huang, shared with CBC Toronto, TD Insurance’s adjuster wrote: “We do not insure the cost of correcting faulty design, material or workmanship.” Damage caused by animals, vandalism or rain also isn't covered in Lawrence Huang's policy, according to the letter.
Semple argues that, in her opinion, the damage to the home was caused by a fraudulent company — but, she says, TD Insurance still isn’t budging on paying for the damage to the roof.

TD Insurance wouldn't speak with CBC Toronto about Huang’s case, citing privacy concerns. But in an email, the company wrote: “TD Insurance recognizes how distressing this situation has been for our client and his family and continues to work directly with them regarding the claim."

Lawrence Huang says he initially tried to live in the basement of his home after the contractor left mid-project, but Toronto Fire Service and city engineers said he had to move out. (Michael Smee/CBC)

Semple says she hired her own adjuster to communicate with the company and some progress has been made. In a follow-up letter dated Sept. 28, TD Insurance said it will cover the damage to the contents after all, but remains adamant that it will not pay for the home’s rebuild.
Until that happens, Huang will continue to live in a motel. Semple says he is covering those costs, but he doesn’t have enough money to rebuild the house.

Luis Seco, a University of Toronto professor who studies the insurance industry, says it’s common for insurers to balk at covering some types of damage, typically structural, which is the most expensive to repair.

items: Home damaged in the GTA storm? Here are your options
A fire destroyed their home. Now they can’t get emergency housing because they have a dog

blocks.text: He says ultimately an insurance company can deny any claim, and the onus is then on the homeowner to take them to court, if they believe the company is violating its policy contract.

But that can be expensive, and he suggests that homeowners first apply to a non-profit insurance industry mediator, the General Insurance Ombudservice, whose members include most Canadian insurance companies.
Police investigating, say roofing scams common
Toronto police acknowledged in an email that it is investigating a fraud complaint at Huang’s property.
Det. David Coffey of the financial crimes unit told CBC Toronto he couldn't comment on Huang’s case specifically, but he said roofing scams are common in the city.
“We’ve been dealing with roofing scams for as long as I've been a police officer, and that’s 29 years,” he said.
Det. David Coffey is with Toronto Police Services' financial crimes unit. He says confidence schemes have cost Torontonians $50 million so far this year. (Mike Smee/CBC)
He said the roofing scam is considered a con game, in which a fraudster builds up a person’s confidence before talking them out of their money.

Typically the scam begins with a salesperson’s knock on the door. The homeowner is warned that a leak in his or her roof is imminent and urgently needs fixing. “They present themselves as the answer to that emergency,” Coffey said. “Your roof is going to leak and the city is going to condemn your house.”
He said most scammers begin by asking for relatively small sums — in the low thousands — and then they escalate the demand until they're convinced the homeowner has nothing left to give.
“It’s really the urgency and the fear they’re generating,” Coffee says. “We’re not reacting intellectually; we’re reacting emotionally.”

So far this year, Coffey says cons of all types have cost Torontonians about $50 million. And that only covers reported scams. TPS figures only about five to 10 percent of victims actually report the crime.
'Bring yourself down off that ledge'
Coffey says the damage done to the Huang home — if it is a fraud — would be “on the higher end” of the typical roofing scam.
His advice? “You need to bring yourself down off that ledge they’ve put you on … Pause and verify. Slow it down and do your own due diligence into that company.”
But he says the best defence is to simply not do business with contractors who come knocking.
“Personally, as a citizen, I wouldn't hire anyone who knocks on my door," Coffey said.
“Urgency these days doesn't mean hurry up. Urgency these days has to mean stop, and verify and talk to your family, talk to other people. Those are the keys.”

articles.title: Stelco's U.S. owner says steelmaker had 'strongest' quarter since acquisition as massive layoffs underway
articles.summary: Stelco's third quarter this year was its "strongest" since the U.S. company acquired it in 2024, according to its owner. At the same time, hundreds in Ontario are set to lose their jobs in Hamilton…

image.caption: Lourenco Goncalves, CEO of U.S.-based Cleveland-Cliffs, is shown in 2022. Goncalves says the steelmaker just completed its best quarter since it was purchased by Cleveland-Cliffs in 2024. (John Kuntz/Associated Press)

blocks.text: Hamilton·New

Stelco's third quarter this year was its "strongest" since the U.S. company acquired it in 2024, according to its owner. At the same time, hundreds in Ontario are set to lose their jobs in Hamilton and Nanticoke. Layoff notices started rolling out earlier this month.
USW local president questions shutdown of some departments if 3rd-quarter results show profitability
Cleveland-Cliffs says Stelco's third quarter this year was its "strongest" since it was acquired by the U.S. company in 2024.
At the same time, hundreds working for the steelmaker in Ontario are set to lose their jobs in Hamilton and Nanticoke. Layoff notices started rolling out earlier this month and are continuing.

"Third quarter was Stelco’s strongest ... since we acquired the company two years ago. The Canadian hot-rolled market has improved substantially," Cleveland-Cliffs CEO Lourenco Goncalves said in a statement Monday.
"However, more needs to be done by the Canadian government to correct a clearly oversupplied market for galvanized steel in Canada."

items: ‘Nowadays, you need a lot fewer people’: Laid-off Stelco workers not alone as steel jobs disappear

blocks.text: Stelco Holdings Inc. said on Sept. 28 it planned to idle part of its Hamilton plant in order to "ensure the survival" of the company as U.S. tariffs has squeezed its sales.

Ron Wells, president of United Steelworkers Local 1005, told CBC that 333 layoffs were expected in Hamilton. USW Local 8782 president John McElroy said up to 50 layoffs are expected at the Lake Erie Works in Nanticoke.

items: 'In a perfect world,' federal government would nationalize Stelco, says Hamilton union leader

blocks.text: During an earnings call Monday, Goncalves said all of Cleveland-Cliffs's major profit drivers increased.

He praised U.S. President Donald Trump's trade policies, saying they are "helping create the conditions needed for companies like ours to continue investing in [local] communities and expanding domestic production," despite Stelco citing tariffs as a key reason for economic struggles.
Steel sales under 'best price environment in 3 years'
In June, Trump signed an executive order applying up to 50 per cent tariffs to certain steel and aluminum imports from Canada.
"We are currently selling steel under the best price environment in three years," said Goncalves.

"These are the prices we need to run a thriving business that grows employment, pays its workers well, reinvests in people and equipment, and protects our critical supply chains and national defence."
Goncalves said the success of the hot-rolled steel business was a direct consequence of the Canadian government's system tariff-rate quota, which limits the amount of product that can be imported.

items: 'In a perfect world,' federal government would nationalize Stelco, says Hamilton union leader

blocks.text: The federal government has said Cleveland-Cliffs's purchase of Stelco included promises to employ "at least the same number of unionized employees and the vast majority of non-unionized employees" as there were in 2024 and through 2029.
Federal Industry Minister Mélanie Joly said "a business decision or even a change in market conditions cannot be used to not follow their commitment."
Goncalves reiterated Stelco's position that the layoffs are a temporary measure until Canada and the U.S. reach a trade agreement.
Stelco steel works in Hamilton are pictured on Oct. 9. The U.S.-based steelmaker announced 300 to 350 layoffs amid the Canada-U.S. trade war. (Evan Mitsui/CBC)
He said the Canadian market is "exposed" and that he has been asking the government to block or "severely reduce" the importing of galvanized steel into the market.
If that happens, he said, "Stelco can immediately bring back all the temporarily laid-off workers."
He also said he's willing to sell Stelco and is prepared to fight the Canadian government in court to preserve the plan to lay off workers.

items: 'Everything is on the table,' Joly says, as Ottawa weighs legal action over Stelco layoffs

blocks.text: Earlier this month, Joly said Ottawa is considering a range of legal options against Cleveland- Cliffs.

The minister said the government is examining its options under Section 40 of the Investment Canada Act. They could include financial penalties, a court order forcing the company to comply with its commitments or an order requiring it to sell its Canadian assets.

items: Cleveland-Cliffs CEO says he's prepared to fight Canada in court over Stelco layoffs

blocks.text: CEO's messaging 'confusing,' union rep says
Wells told CBC Hamilton on Monday that workers are feeling "underappreciated" as layoffs proceed.
"They're dedicated, loyal employees" he said. "They work weekends, they work holidays, they missed their kids' hockey games, graduations, and that loyalty isn't being repaid."
Wells also called Goncalves's messaging "confusing."
"He said Stelco's Q3 results were good, they're profitable. If they're profitable, why'd he shut down our [cold-rolled] and coated [steel] departments?" Wells said.
He also noted that Cleveland-Cliffs is advocating for a reduction in foreign imports, adding that "the U.S. [and] Cleveland-Cliffs might be part of that problem" as a large steel importer to Canada.
"We still hope Minister Joly follows through with her commitment to enforce the Investment Canada Act," Wells said.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Aura Carreño Rosas is a reporter at CBC Hamilton. She's originally from Venezuela. She has extensive experience in covering stories about immigrants and migrant workers as well as interesting people with diverse journeys. You can contact her at aura.carreno.rosas@cbc.ca

articles.title: Incoming Quebec premier asks lieutenant-governor to skip cabinet's swearing-in
articles.summary: In a letter sent Monday to Lt.-Gov. Manon Jeannotte, the Parti Québécois leader stated his incoming government will not allow a representative of the British Crown to preside over the event.

image.caption: PQ Leader Paul St-Pierre Plamondon has already stated he will once again refuse to swear allegiance to King Charles. (Sylvain Roy Roussel/Radio-Canada)

blocks.text: Montreal·New
In a letter sent Monday to Lt.-Gov. Manon Jeannotte, the Parti Québécois leader stated his incoming government will not allow a representative of the British Crown to preside over the event.
Court to hear emergency bid to force newly elected Quebec politicians to swear oath to monarch
Quebec premier-designate Paul St-Pierre Plamondon has formally asked the province's lieutenant-governor to stay away from his new cabinet’s swearing-in ceremony on Wednesday.
"We firmly intend to abolish this monarchy in Quebec, both within our democratic institutions and in our civil society," St-Pierre Plamondon wrote.

He makes it clear that he does not want the lieutenant-governor present, requesting that she sign the necessary appointment documents behind the scenes so the Secretary General can administer the oaths without her. Proceeding this way, the PQ leader wrote, will allow the newly appointed ministers to begin their work immediately.

“We thank you in advance for the co-operation you will demonstrate to ensure that this important day for our democracy unfolds without hindrance and with respect for the will of the elected members of the National Assembly of Quebec,” he added.
But the new government's anti-monarchy agenda is facing an immediate legal roadblock.
One of the lawyers challenging the 2022 Quebec law that made the mandatory oath to the King optional for elected officials says his case for an emergency injunction will be heard in court Tuesday.
Lawrence David said in an email he expects a quick decision from Judge Ian Demers, but "we will 100 per cent appeal the judgment if we do not win."
To swear or not to swear allegiance

Earlier this month, David, founder of the Public Interest Litigation Institute, filed an emergency injunction in an attempt to force the incoming Parti Québécois (PQ) government to swear allegiance to King Charles.

The injunction asks the court to immediately suspend a 2022 provincial law, known as Bill 4, that made the oath to the monarch optional for members of the National Assembly. David already filed a lawsuit in August over the same matter.

items: Injunction filed to force incoming PQ government to take oath to King

blocks.text: Bill 4 added a clause to the Constitution Act of 1867 stating that the oath to the monarch no longer applies to Quebec legislators.

The bill was tabled by the Coalition Avenir Québec government after facing pressure from the PQ. Several members of the PQ had refused to swear allegiance to King Charles III and were barred from sitting.
Will the PQ be barred from their seats?

The legal challenge comes on the heels of the provincial election, which handed the Parti Québécois a minority government. St-Pierre Plamondon has already stated he will once again refuse to swear allegiance to King Charles.
If the stay is granted, incoming MNAs who refuse the oath could be legally barred from taking their seats when the legislature reconvenes in mid-November.

At the heart of the lawsuit is the argument that Quebec unilaterally altered the 1867 Constitution Act without the required unanimous consent of the House of Commons, the Senate and all of the country’s provincial legislatures to abolish the mandatory oath.

items: PQ leader readies team for the work ahead as members sworn in at National Assembly

blocks.text: It also alleges the law violates Section 3 of the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms, which guarantees the right to effective representation, because politicians who do not take the oath are not qualified to serve as an MNA.
David has warned that if the newly elected government attempts to unilaterally abolish the office of the lieutenant-governor, he is prepared to launch additional legal challenges.
Written by Isaac Olson

articles.title: Up to 2M passengers in seaports expected for Undas 2026, says PCG
articles.summary: The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) said Tuesday that up to two million sea passengers are expected to travel during the observance of Undas 2026, similar to the recorded volume last year.

blocks.text: Published October 20, 2026 3:35pm
The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) said Tuesday that up to two million sea passengers are expected to travel during the observance of Undas 2026, similar to the recorded volume last year.
PCG spokesperson Commodore Noemie Cayabyab said around 17,000 personnel will be deployed nationwide, together with the agency’s sea and air assets and radio equipment.

“Last year po… halos 1.5 million po ang ating na-monitor na byahero sa lahat po ng pantalan. So this year we will be anticipating the same number or baka maglaro pa po ito hanggang 2 million na pasahero,” Caybyab said in a Bagong Pilipinas Ngayon briefing.
(Last year, we monitored nearly 1.5 million travelers across all ports. So this year, we are anticipating the same number, or it could even reach up to 2 million passengers.)
Caybyab said the Coast Guard, including its stations and substations, will be placed on heightened alert status from October 29 to November 3 in anticipation of the influx of passengers at seaports.
PCG will also activate its deployable response group composed of rescue swimmers and medical nurses to assist travelers.
According to the Coast Guard, under heightened alert status, passengers can expect stricter security and safety measures, from port inspections to observing safety compliance on vessels.

“We will be intensifying the conduct of the pre-departure inspection. So ibig sabihin po niyan, we will not allow any vessels po na magsasakay ng lagpas na pasahero sa kanilang itinakdang kapasidad,” Caybayab said.
(We will be intensifying the conduct of pre-departure inspections. This means we will not allow any vessel to board passengers beyond its authorized carrying capacity.)
“Maglalagay rin po tayo ng ating mga Coast Guard K-9 dogs sa lahat po ng major ports para po mag-asiste sa pagco-conduct ng security inspection, particularly po sa ating mga bagahe,” she added.
(We will also deploy Coast Guard K-9 dogs to all major ports to assist in conducting security inspections, particularly for baggage.)
The PCG advised passengers who will board at major ports to arrive at least two to three hours before their scheduled departure to avoid delays due to thorough inspections.

The agency also encouraged travelers on board to report if they experience any safety violations, such as a failure to conduct safety briefings on the boat, using QR codes displayed inside the vessels.
To ensure passenger safety, Cayabyab said assistance desks will be set up at ports where passengers can inquire about travel details, request medical assistance, or report emergencies.
Typhoon

Meanwhile, following the entry of Super Typhoon Rosal in the Philippine Area of Responsibility. the PCG said it is continuously monitoring forecasts and coordinating with the Philippine Ports Authority (PPA) for possible trip cancellations.
“Patuloy rin po ang ating pagbabantay at pagmo-monitor sa nilalabas na weather update ng PAGASA,” Cayabyab said.
(We are also continuously monitoring the weather updates issued by PAGASA.)

“‘Pag may itataaas na po na Wind Signal, kahit Wind Signal No.1 lang po ito… ang barko po, ang pantalan na panggagalingan at pupuntahan po ng mga barko… definitely ica-cancel po natin o isu-suspend po natin lahat ng trips nila,” she added.
(Once a Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal is raised—even if it is only Wind Signal No. 1—trips for vessels originating from or heading to affected ports will definitely be canceled or suspended.)
The PCG advised all passengers to check the weather forecast before leaving home on the day of their trip.
The public was also warned against riding colorum motorboats, as these lack proper life-saving equipment, which could compromise the safety of its passenger. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: Second Senate resolution seeking China ambassador's expulsion filed
articles.summary: Sen. Risa Hontiveros has formally urged President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to declare Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan persona non grata, or else ask Beijing to recall him.

blocks.text: October 20, 2026 | 3:32pm
Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan during his meeting with Davao City Mayor Baste Duterte on Jan. 26, 2026.
Davao City Mayor Baste Duterte via Facebook
MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Risa Hontiveros has formally urged President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to declare Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan persona non grata, or else ask Beijing to recall him.
Hers is the second Senate resolution in two days seeking action on the diplomat over his remark that China “may easily win” if it used force.
Senate Resolution 746, filed Tuesday, October 20, comes a day after a similar measure by Sen. Erwin Tulfo on Monday.

While Tulfo’s resolution asks the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) “to recommend to the appropriate authorities” that Jing be declared persona non grata, Hontiveros' resolution wants the Senate “to urge the President of the Philippines to declare Ambassador Jing Quan of the People’s Republic of China persona non grata, or, in the alternative, to request his recall.”
The Senate does not have the power to expel a foreign diplomat or declare an envoy persona non grata. This action can be done only by the executive branch, specifically the president or the DFA.
Jing made the remark in question at a forum on October 15. He was asked about Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. calling China a regional “troublemaker.”
“If we want to use force, we may easily win. But no, we will not use force,” he said, adding that the Philippines should feel fortunate to have China as a neighbor.

The DFA said the remark seemed to convey a “thinly veiled threat of the use of force.” Later, Marcos said he would be seeking a discussion with the ambassador, as it “sounds very much to me like a threat.”

Foreign Affairs Secretary Theresa Lazaro summoned Jing on Monday to convey Manila’s strong objection to his words. The same day, Palace Press Officer Claire Castro appeared to be toning down the Palace's reaction and said Marcos “would not want" a persona non grata tag against any foreign envoy in the country.
Jing has denied that his remarks were a threat and has accused the Philippine side of taking his words out of context.

Hontiveros’ resolution acknowledges “the primacy of the President in the conduct of the nation’s foreign affairs.” It says the Senate “nevertheless wishes to express its disapproval of the undiplomatic conduct of a foreign envoy.”

It argues that “Ambassador Jing’s claim of restraint is belied by the conduct of the Chinese government in the West Philippine Sea" with its ships and aerial assets persistently harassing those of the Philippines'.

“This is not the first time the Chinese government’s words have failed to align with its actions,” the resolution says. It cites a July video by state-owned China Daily “depicting a monkey in a barong taking orders from the United States and Japan.”
Tulfo, for his part, said in an interview with reporters on Monday: “Why wait for persona non grata? Just go home.”

articles.title: Getting Ziggy with it: David Bowie’s alter egos inspire dance show that will transform his songs
articles.summary:
Subject to Change: A Dance for David Bowie will explore how the musician ‘practised a form of artistic reincarnation’, says choreographer Marcos Morau

‘Let’s dance,” sang David Bowie in…

blocks.text: ‘Let’s dance,” sang David Bowie in 1983, commanding: “Put on your red shoes and dance the blues.” That call is to be answered – with footwear TBC – by an international dance production featuring new choral arrangements of songs from throughout his career.

Subject to Change: A Dance for David Bowie will be staged at Sadler’s Wells in London in autumn 2028 after a world premiere in Luxembourg. It will visit Tokyo in 2029. The show will explore how Bowie “practised a form of artistic reincarnation” according to Spanish choreographer Marcos Morau who is taking inspiration from the superstar’s transformations into personas such as Aladdin Sane and the Thin White Duke.

“One of the greatest dangers for an artist is ending up resembling themselves too much,” said Morau. “Bowie turned change into a way of remaining true to himself. That inspires me deeply. I believe every new work should force us to let go of some certainty. Art shouldn’t serve to confirm who we are, but rather to accept that life transforms us, that we change over time, and that our own contradictions help us grow.”

blocks.caption: ‘What happens when his songs leave behind the voice we all know?’ … Bowie in his Thin White Duke era in 1976. Photograph: Jorgen Angel/Redferns

blocks.text: Orchestrations of pop and rock classics have powered recent hit dance productions such as Black Sabbath: The Ballet and a reworking of The Who’s Quadrophenia, bringing in new audiences. In Subject to Change, Bowie’s songs will be interwoven with choral sounds from around the world and the voice of Spanish singer Maria Arnal. “I’m not interested in reproducing Bowie or creating a nostalgic tribute,” said Morau, who wants to explore “what happens when his songs leave behind the voice we all know and travel towards other voices, other cultures and other generations”. By employing different choral traditions, he hopes to “transform something deeply individual into a collective experience. I like to think that a work of art remains alive as long as we are able to transform it, and that perhaps the best way to remain faithful to Bowie is to dare to change him.”

Over his career, Bowie collaborated with significant choreographers including Édouard Lock and Annie-B Parson. He was taught dance by the great mime Lindsay Kemp who recalled him taking part in improvisations such as sailors drowning at sea. Kemp directed Bowie in a 1967 theatre show, Pierrot in Turquoise, and tried – but failed – to get him to play Puss in Boots.

The pierrot became one of Bowie’s alter egos – others included Halloween Jack from his Diamond Dogs era and, most famously, Ziggy Stardust, the intergalactic rockstar who “took it all too far but, boy, could he play guitar”. A black vinyl jumpsuit with stripes known as Tokyo Pop, designed by Kansai Yamamoto for Bowie to wear as Ziggy in 1973, is used in the promotional image for Subject to Change.

blocks.caption: The Subject to Change promotional image featuring the Tokyo Pop costume designed by Kansai Yamamoto Photograph: Kazuyoshi Shimomura

blocks.text: Each of his alter egos ushered in a new musical direction and a fresh look for Bowie but also brought out a different physicality, said Morau. “For Bowie, the body was just as important as the music or the costumes. It wasn’t simply a matter of appearance, but of how he inhabited space. What fascinates me is that he managed to turn his own body into a territory of fiction, allowing those fictions to become part of reality. When you can transform yourself with that kind of freedom, you can also find new ways of living. In a world obsessed with categorising us and making us follow certain patterns, Bowie turned his body into an act of defiance.”

blocks.caption: ‘Perhaps the best way to remain faithful to Bowie is to dare to change him’ … Marcos Morau. Photograph: Kazuyoshi Shimomura

blocks.text: Morau is an in-demand choreographer whose works include Horses (2024), created for Nederlands Dans Theater, which featured animalistic dancers prowling around mean streets to music by contemporary classical composer Caroline Shaw. Étude, performed earlier this year by the Paris Opera Ballet, upended the conventions of ballet. The former piece featured dancers wielding giant lamp posts; the latter used a swinging replica of the chandelier in the auditorium of Paris’s Palais Garnier. Both sets were designed by Max Glaenzel who will work on Subject to Change. The costumes will be by another of Morau’s regular collaborators, Silvia Delagneau, and the musical direction is by Alex Röser Vatiché and Ben Meerwein. It is co-produced by Sadler’s Wells, Bunkamura in Japan and Morau’s company La Veronal.

Ten years after Bowie’s death, the musician continues to fascinate. Earlier this year, a 3D documentary about him was unveiled at the Venice film festival. David Bowie: You’re Not Alone, an hour-long immersive portrait, is running at Lightroom in London and the V&A’s Bowie archive, featuring Yamamoto’s costumes for Ziggy Stardust, goes on tour next month.

Last weekend, Let’s Dance inspired a paso doble on Strictly. What is Morau’s favourite Bowie song to dance to? “Space Oddity – it’s probably not the most obvious choice for dancing, but that’s precisely why I like it,” he said. “There’s something profoundly choreographic about imagining a body losing gravity and drifting away from everything familiar.”

articles.title: Healey to reject calls to raise capital gains tax in budget
articles.summary:
Cabinet colleagues have previously called for an increase but chancellor feels it might ultimately cost the Treasury

John Healey will not raise

blocks.text: John Healey will not raise capital gains tax in next week’s budget, despite previous calls to do so from cabinet colleagues including Louise Haigh and Wes Streeting.
The chancellor has decided that any increase might ultimately cost the Treasury if wealthy individuals defer the sale of assets or move them out of the country, according to Treasury sources.

The tax is imposed on profits that individuals make when they sell assets that have increased in value, such as second homes or shares. The decision not to increase CGT, first reported by the FT and the Times, will mean the chancellor’s main revenue raiser is likely to be raising tax on banks’ profits.
In a speech last month, Healey said he wanted to prioritise wealth creation without it being constantly subject to penalties.

“I recognise that the cost of business – that’s energy bills, regulation burdens, planning constraints, labour costs – have grown since Covid. And I want to draw the line,” he said. “And whether it is the cost of business or the cost of living, the only way we deal with these in the long term is growth.
“I want to see this country as a country of wealth creation. I want our government decisions and policies to raise the levels of confidence and investment and profit in British business.”

In the race to replace Keir Starmer as prime minister, several senior Labour figures had suggested a route to equalising capital gains with income tax rates, including Haigh, now the now first secretary of state.

Streeting, now the defence secretary, who considered running against Burnham to replace Starmer, had also suggested a rise, calling it a “wealth tax that works”. He said the current system meant a growing gap between earned income and unearned income.

Instead, Healey is poised to tax Britain’s banks in his budget on 28 October, amid strong earnings on the back of rising interest rates, with the UK’s four largest lenders – HSBC, NatWest, Barclays and Lloyds Banking Group – alone having generated £200bn in pre-tax profits over the past five years.

Healey is reported to be willing to accept a reduction in the fiscal headroom left by his predecessor, Rachel Reeves. The UK’s cost of borrowing has risen sharply in recent weeks, alongside that of other big economies, which analysts have suggested could as much as halve the £24bn cushion Reeves had built up against Labour’s fiscal rules at the time of the last spring forecast.
The Conservative leader, Kemi Badenoch, will give a speech on Tuesday saying the government should cut its spending plans instead of raising taxes, including cuts to welfare and the civil service.

“We have to stop borrowing so much. But instead of doing that, Labour are taking out loans to pay the interest on our loans,” she will say. “Any family or business in that position would know they were sinking, that every attempt to borrow their way out was pulling them deeper. The right way is to bring spending down now.

“Cuts are never easy, but they are much easier if what you are doing is based on fairness. Fairness to taxpayers, fairness to future generations and fairness to those who really need support. Under our golden economic rule, half of the savings we have made would go to reducing the deficit.”

articles.title: Senate reso urges Marcos to declare Chinese envoy Jing Quan persona non grata
articles.summary: Senator Risa Hontiveros on Tuesday filed a resolution calling on President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. to declare Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan persona non grata or request his recall by the…

blocks.text: Published October 20, 2026 3:26pm

Senator Risa Hontiveros on Tuesday filed a resolution calling on President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. to declare Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan persona non grata or request his recall by the Chinese government, following the latter’s “use of force” remark.

Under proposed Senate Resolution No. 746, Hontiveros said that even as the Senate recognizes the primacy of the President in the conduct of the nation’s foreign affairs, the chamber “nevertheless wishes to express its disapproval of the undiplomatic conduct of a foreign envoy, to inform the President’s exercise of the authority granted by the Constitution.”

“[U]nder the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, to which the Philippines and China are parties, a receiving State may notify the sending State ‘at any time and without having to explain its decision’ that its head of mission is persona non grata, thus obliging the sending State (to) recall the envoy or terminate his functions,” the resolution read.

The resolution was filed a day after Malacañang said that Marcos is not keen on making any declaration against the Chinese ambassador despite his contentious statement that Beijing could “easily win” if it resorts to force against the Philippines.
But the President earlier said that Jing’s remark “sounds very much like a threat,” and is “not a very diplomatic statement to be made.”
On Monday, the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) formally summoned Jing to convey the Philippine's "serious concern and strong objection" to his recent remarks.

A similar resolution was also filed by Senator Erwin Tulfo, vice chairperson of the Senate committee on foreign relations, calling on the DFA to recommend declaring the Chinese Ambassador persona non grata.

Under proposed Senate Resolution No. 739, Tulfo said that Jing’s remark “raised serious concerns over the propriety of diplomatic conduct and its implications for Philippine sovereignty and national security.” — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: Japan probe sets course for Mars moon
articles.summary: The MMX spacecraft is on its way to Mars' moon Phobos to collect surface samples that could help answer long-standing questions about the formation of the Solar System.

image.caption: Thousands of people tuned into the livestream of the launch despite the early hour in JapanImage: Kyodo/REUTERS

blocks.text: A Japanese spacecraft successfully set off on a journey to one of Mars' moons late Monday in a race to become the first mission to return samples to Earth and potentially unlock the mysterious origins of the Solar System.

The uncrewed Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is expected to reach Mars in August 2027. It will attempt to collect samples from Phobos, the larger of the planet's two moons, and deploy the German-French rover IDEFIX to explore the surface.
Pioneering mission heads to Mars moon — and back

The flagship H3 rocket carrying the MMX probe lifted off into a pitch-black sky from the Tanegashima Space Center at 4:41 a.m. local time (1941 GMT Monday), the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) said.

Flight controllers burst into applause and jumped to their feet as the spacecraft blasted into space, shaking hands and embracing. Thousands of people tuned in to watch the livestream despite the early hour.
An hour later, JAXA announced that the probe had successfully separated from the H3 rocket and was "beginning its journey towards the Martian system."
"I'd dreamt of this day, so I'm incredibly happy," said JAXA scientist Mari Aida. "Right now I feel really relieved."
The agency also received signals from the spacecraft as expected, confirming it was operating normally.
Making way for science
Scientists hope the probe's discoveries will help lay the groundwork for eventual human exploration.

"The samples from MMX will bring forth paradigm-shifting science on the Mars system for generations to come, especially as NASA prepares to send the first humans to Mars," Nicky Fox, administrator of NASA's Science Mission Directorate, said in a message broadcast on the JAXA live stream.

blocks.caption: The mission is a collaboration with US and European space agencies, as well as numerous universities and tech companiesImage: Kyodo/REUTERS

blocks.text: JAXA also hopes the mission will reveal how Mars and its two moons formed, unlocking a key piece of knowledge about the formation of the Solar System.

One theory holds that Mars' two moons formed after a giant celestial body collided with the planet. Another hypothesis suggests the moons are asteroids captured by Mars' gravity. Confirming either theory would help scientists determine "how a habitable environment for life might have arisen on the terrestrial planets," JAXA said, referring to the four rocky planets closest to the sun.
Probe to reach destination in August 2027
The probe is due to arrive near Mars around August 2027, where it will orbit one of the planet's two natural moons, Phobos.

A French-German rover named IDEFIX, after the dog from the Asterix comic series, will be the first vehicle to travel across Phobos to conduct surface observations and help ensure a safe landing for the Japanese probe. It is no bigger than a microwave oven.

Once MMX arrives on Phobos, it will spend about two hours collecting at least 10 grams of material from the moon's surface before launching back into space. It will also study Mars' other natural moon, Deimos, during a series of flybys before leaving the Martian region in 2030.

blocks.caption: Phobos, the larger of the two Martian moons, orbits the planet three times a dayImage: JAXA/DLR/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Another objective of the mission is to explore the possibility of using Phobos as a "natural space station" by establishing the requirements for a round trip.
Phobos is a lumpy, potato-shaped rock measuring about 22 kilometers (14 miles) across.
The mission, which aims to complete the first round trip to the Martian region, is a collaboration involving US and European space agencies along with several private technology companies.

US and Chinese space agencies have also been competing to become the first to return rock samples from the surface of Mars to Earth. NASA's Perseverance rover, which has been exploring the planet since 2021, has already collected samples. The return mission, however, was canceled by US President Donald Trump's administration after a congressional vote in January.

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Posts promising cash aid, rice subsidy for all national ID holders are fake
articles.summary: The links to the alleged list of areas covered by the supposed nationwide program lead to a third-party blog site to trick social media users into typing in sensitive personal information

blocks.text: Claim: All national ID holders, including non-Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps) beneficiaries, are eligible to receive a cash aid and rice subsidy starting October 20.
Why we fact-checked this: The claim was posted by Facebook page Ph News Alert 24 on October 19. The page currently has over 26,000 followers.
As of writing, the video containing the claim has amassed over 42,400 reactions, 11,600 comments, 9,000 shares, and 3.2 million views.
The video shows a host of a supposed news organization detailing the registration process for the program. Graphics on the video also show October 20, 22, 29, and 30 as the supposed payout dates.

“Lahat ng may national ID ay merong makukuhang P5,000 at rice subsidy. Lahat ng Filipino… Ang registration form ay makikita dito sa aming post at comment section. Kapag nakapag-register ka na, i-comment ang pangalan ng mayor niyo para matawagan namin kaagad,” the host said.

(Everyone with a national ID will receive P5,000 and a rice subsidy. All Filipinos… The registration form can be found here in our post and in the comment section. Once you have registered, comment the name of your mayor here so we can call right away.)
The posts encourage social media users to share the video to spread the alleged good news. The page has also reposted the same claim multiple times, each racking up thousands of views.

The facts: There is no nationwide cash aid and rice subsidy distribution program for all Filipinos who have a national ID. The Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) earlier released an advisory on May 7 debunking claims that all national ID holders are automatically eligible to receive certain benefits promised in various AI-generated videos.

“Ang pagkakaroon nito [national ID] ay hindi nangangahulugan ng awtomatikong pagtanggap ng anumang uri ng ayuda o assistance. Ang pagbibigay ng benepisyo ay nananatiling nakabatay sa umiiral na patakaran, proseso, at kwalipikasyon ng bawat ahensya na nagpapatupad ng mga programang ito,” the advisory reads.

(Possessing a national ID does not automatically guarantee the receipt of any form of aid or assistance. The granting of benefits remains subject to the existing policies, processes, and qualification requirements of each agency implementing these programs.)

The video itself is also AI-generated. Results from the detection tool HiveModeration flagged it as 68.2% likely to be an AI-generated video and 96.7% likely to include AI-generated audio. It also scored 83% likelihood on UndetectableAI.
Fake links: The links in the caption and comment section redirect users to a fake registration form embedded in a blog website — not an official government website.

Phishing link checking tool EasyDMARC flagged the link as suspicious. Using such sites and providing sensitive personal information may expose users to identity theft and other scams. (READ: Phishing 101: How to spot and avoid phishing)
Rappler has previously debunked fake links to alleged cash aid and rice subsidy registration websites:

items: FACT CHECK: Post offering cash, livelihood aid under Bong Go’s name is fake
FACT CHECK: Impostor Facebook group shares fake DSWD cash aid offers
FACT CHECK: UPLIFT aid is for eligible beneficiaries, not all Filipinos with valid IDs
FACT CHECK: UPLIFT program does not offer P5,000 cash aid, rice subsidy to all Filipinos
FACT CHECK: DSWD not offering cash aid to senior citizens through Facebook
FACT CHECK: Online registration links for DSWD, DepEd student aid programs are fake
FACT CHECK: No free electricity, subsidies for national ID, vaccine card holders

blocks.text: – Lourence Angelo Marcellana/Rappler.com

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.title: US gave us no warning of Russian strikes on Kyiv power plants, Zelenskyy says
articles.summary:
Ukrainian president accuses Washington of ‘denial of reality’ in continuing row with Trump over apparent support for Moscow

Ukraine did not receive a warning from the US about an impending…

blocks.text: Ukraine did not receive a warning from the US about an impending Russian missile attack on Sunday evening, Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said, reviving concerns that Washington is withholding intelligence to bully Kyiv into capitulating to Moscow.

Yuri Ihnat, a spokesperson for the Ukrainian air force, said on television on Monday morning that Ukraine had not received a warning before a Russian missile barrage hit power plants in Kyiv at about 11pm. Earlier, a Ukrainian government official had told the Guardian the US had not warned the capital about the impending missile strike.
Ukraine did receive a warning before a subsequent strike, at 3am, Ihnat added.

“Once again, Russia launched a ballistic missile attack in multiple waves throughout the night, and once again, there was no warning from our partners,” Zelenskyy wrote in a social media post on Monday morning.

“When the supply of missiles for Ukrainian air defence is blocked, and Russia receives sanctions relief or delays, it is, unfortunately, a denial of reality on the part of our partners,” the president added.
Zelenskyy is grappling with recent US moves benefiting the Russian president, Vladimir Putin.

On Friday, Donald Trump waived a sweeping package of sanctions on Russia, telling Congress the pause on the legislation, named after the late senator Lindsey Graham and passed by both chambers, was in the national interest. Ukraine has also complained of slowed deliveries of PAC-3 air defence missiles from the US.

The US president wrote on Truth Social on Sunday: “My decision on Russia is a very simple one. I am in the process of negotiating peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don’t want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table.
“Zelenskyy doesn’t care, and frankly, with all of the money that Europe is famously giving him … he doesn’t want to end this war, and probably never did.”

Trump also told reporters on Monday that he would consider a trilateral meeting with Russia and China. He said: “We ‌would have it to talk about nuclear weapons and denuclearisation. If ‌President Xi wants to have it, I’d ​have it.”

For years, the US has warned Ukraine before Russia launched ballistic missiles, giving authorities several minutes to sound alarms and allow civilians to reach shelters before the strikes hit. However, Ukraine has said it was not warned on at least three days in the past week before missiles were launched, amid a public quarrel between Zelenskyy and Trump.

Speaking in the early hours of Monday on a trip to Samarkand, Uzbekistan, the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, said: “If it happened last night, I don’t know exactly. I know a few nights ago there was a software problem involving their early warning system.”

US officials have not previously mentioned a software glitch in the early warning system. In at least one case, Ukrainian officials had been told that bad weather over southern Russia had obscured preparations for the missile launch. Rubio said the military’s European Command was looking into the strikes.

The US has maintained plausible deniability as services and programmes provided to support Ukraine have suddenly begun to fail. The Trump administration has denied that it throttled services in Ukraine for Starlink, the satellite internet service run by Elon Musk that is used both on offensive drones and anti-air weapons by Ukraine.

Ukraine has also said US weapons delivered through the PURL scheme, where Europe purchases US weapons then delivers them to Ukraine, have been delayed. The Trump administration reportedly threatened Kyiv with a slowdown in crucial weapons deliveries unless it stopped striking Russian oil refineries.
On Sunday, Ukraine launched more than 1,000 drones at Russia in one of its largest aerial attacks of the war, setting fire to an oil export terminal and a depot in St Petersburg.

The Russian barrage on Sunday evening hit 28 substations and other critical energy facilities, depriving more than 500,000 people of electricity, heat and running water, Zelenskyy said on social media. Russia has sought to disrupt daily life in Ukraine by attacking trains, shopping centres, fuel stations and supermarkets, among other sites.
Russia fired 16 ballistic missiles at Kyiv and the surrounding region, Zelenskyy said, and officials in the capital reported that a 21-year-old woman had been killed.

Later drone strikes on a public park in the north-eastern Kharkiv region killed six people, including young children. The regional governor, Oleg Synegubov, said on Telegram that three of the dead in the attack on Nova Vodolaha were children, including one in a pushchair. Seven children were among the 14 wounded. Police posted pictures showing damaged playground equipment.

Synegubov condemned “another terrorist act by the Russian Federation”, saying “the enemy strikes a recreational park in the middle of the day, knowing that there is no military infrastructure there at all”.

Pope Leo XIV spoke by phone with Zelenskyy on Monday to discuss the embattled city of Oleshky in Ukraine’s Kherson region, according to a Vatican statement. He told the Ukrainian president that he had asked Putin for a humanitarian ceasefire during a call with the Russian leader on Friday.

Residents of Oleshky face a worsening humanitarian crisis, with shortages of food and medication, as they are caught in the crossfire between Russian and Ukrainian troops. The Vatican said that Leo had expressed deep concern about conditions in the city and sought a ceasefire to permit aid deliveries and evacuations.
The call to Zelenskyy came two days after Leo, 71, was discharged from a hospital in Rome where he underwent a lung cancer operation on Tuesday.
The Kremlin said on Friday it had explained to Leo what it called “the Kyiv regime’s responsibility for the difficult humanitarian situation”.

articles.title: China sends naval forces to monitor US warship near disputed shoal
articles.summary: The Chinese military's Southern Theater Command asserts that the US warship 'illegally intruded' into waters adjacent to a shoal in the Spratly Islands

blocks.text: US-CHINA RIVALRY. US and Chinese flags are seen in this illustration created on April 10, 2025
Dado Ruvic/Reuters
The Chinese military's Southern Theater Command asserts that the US warship 'illegally intruded' into waters adjacent to a shoal in the Spratly Islands
BEIJING, China – China’s military said on Tuesday, October 20, it had sent forces to watch a US warship that “illegally” entered waters around a disputed shoal in the South China Sea.

China views almost all of the busy waterway as its own territory, despite overlapping claims by Brunei, Malaysia, the Philippines, Taiwan, and Vietnam, with recent tension most pronounced between Beijing and Manila.

The Chinese military’s Southern Theater Command said the Charleston “illegally intruded” into waters adjacent to Sabina (Escoda) Shoal in the Spratly Islands without Chinese government approval in the early hours of Tuesday.

blocks.caption: Senate resolution seeks to declare Chinese envoy ‘persona non grata’

blocks.text: “The US action infringes upon China’s sovereign rights and interests, jeopardizes maritime security, and is detrimental to regional peace and stability,” it said.
“The US side should immediately cease such activities.”
China’s navy dispatched forces to track and monitor the ship, it added.

The US Navy did not immediately respond to a request for comment. It generally refers to such missions as “freedom of navigation operations,” though its last known one in the South China Sea was more than a year ago.
Last month, a China Coast Guard vessel rammed a Philippine boat on a refueling mission near the same shoal.
China and the Philippines, which has a mutual defense treaty with the US, both contest sovereignty over Sabina Shoal and the entire Spratly Islands archipelago. – Rappler.com

articles.title: French cities calm overnight after curfews imposed to quell violence, PM says
articles.summary: Sébastien Lecornu said new curfews for Tuesday night would be decided where necessary.

blocks.text: Targeted curfews across France contributed to a quiet night following a weekend of riots and looting across the country, the Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has said.
Curfews were introduced across parts of central Paris, including Place de la République, where protesters had gathered over the weekend, and the Les Halles shopping area.

Other measures restricting the movement of young people and gatherings were introduced in cities such as Marseille, Bordeaux, Nice and Lyon in the south, as well as Lille and other towns in the north.
Lecornu thanked police officers and gendarmes for enforcing the measures, adding that further curfews on Tuesday night would be decided depending on where they are necessary.
Writing in a post on X, he said decisions would be made "on the ground" by French regions and local mayors.

articles.title: She was harassed for crude remarks about Modi at a Cockroach protest. Now she can’t leave home
articles.summary:
​After a protest clip went viral, a teenager’s life was torn apart by threats that sent her and her family into hiding. Plus, a book on citizen journalism

Before 24 July, a person I will…

blocks.text: Before 24 July, a person I will call R was preoccupied with the ordinary routines of teenage life: experimenting with makeup, grumbling over mathematics homework and hanging out with friends at a tea stall.

That month, as the fever of student protests spread across the country, the 15-year-old watched on her phone as young people poured into Jantar Mantar, the designated protest site in Delhi, demanding education reform. She went too. But an 11-second video clip from the protest site, in which she made crude and profane remarks about the prime minister, Narendra Modi, upended her life.

“I feel like a criminal, as if I murdered someone,” R said in her first interview about life since the backlash. “I didn’t get a chance to make amends. In my own country, I am being treated like an enemy.”
It’s been 86 days since that protest, but R doesn’t leave home over safety concerns, trapped in the reality the ordeal created.

The summer agitation had for weeks demanded the ousting of the then-education minister, Dharmendra Pradhan, over repeated examination paper leaks. But after a violent police crackdown on a student march the anger spilled over to the Modi government.

I went to Jantar Mantar every night that week as people from all walks of life streamed in. Protest signs once directed largely against Pradhan now increasingly targeted Modi and his powerful deputy, Amit Shah, whose ministry controls Delhi Police.

The language was often profane and sexualised, and was quickly seized on by government supporters to condemn the protesters. Pro-government media channels ran heated debates about the disrespectful language and questioned the motives of those gathered. Women were singled out; BJP supporters identified them from social media clips and doxed them.

R found herself at the centre of this storm. A police case was filed against her for insult intended to provoke a breach of the peace, and statements that could lead to public mischief and defamation. The complainant told Scroll, an independent news organisation, that she had called R and asked her to publicly apologise.

After Pradhan resigned, Modi posted on Instagram about the use of vulgar abuses against him by “some mischievous children”, saying: “It is a cultural shock. How can our daughters speak like this?” Modi added that the children must be forgiven, instead of being punished.

Meanwhile, R issued an apology to Modi. In a grainy video filmed in low light, R stands against a dull white wall wearing a striped T-shirt, her hands folded in a namaste. “I am so ashamed of saying those things that I am not even able to raise my eyes. I apologise to the whole nation for it. This is my first and last mistake,” she said. (Local media reported that the complainant withdrew the police case after R’s video was posted.)
“I cried after making that video,” she told me. “I was feeling so helpless.”

But her apology did little to stem the abuse. She received rape and death threats, abusive phone calls, incessant warnings on text, knocks on doors and cars outside her apartment building in a Delhi suburb.

“I couldn’t understand what was happening,” R said, her eyes misting up as she recalled the initial days after the incident. “People older than my mother were calling me randi (prostitute), aatankwadi (terrorist), deshdrohi (enemy of the state). Others were offering Rs11,000 to find me and Rs21,000 to beat me.”

With her phone and address leaked, R and her mother were compelled to leave their home. They struggled to find landlords willing to rent them a place to stay. They found one apartment, then another and then another. Her mother, a single parent, lost the income she earned from tutoring. To pay for the repeated moves, she sold her gold jewellery. That money is keeping them afloat. She estimates it will probably last another four months. As the clock runs out, her mother is desperately searching for work.
During this time, R has not been to school and can no longer imagine returning. Some friends have cut off contact, leaving her increasingly isolated.

Despite her apology video, pro-government media continued to hound her, she said. In late August, frustrated and angry at yet another media crew showing up, she uploaded a video to social media laying bare what she was going through.
“Modiji, my life has become hell,” R said addressing the prime minister. “Now I can’t go anywhere, neither do I have any freedom. I can’t live anywhere. I have to live hiding my face,” she said.
R told me she wants people to understand how traumatising her experience has been. “To make someone homeless overnight is a big deal,” she said.

Now, stuck indoors, she is watching another wave of protests unfold. This time it’s over the controversial electoral rolls revision that has removed 130 million voters from the register. (If you missed it, read last week’s newsletter about this issue.)

R feels solidarity with the students getting brutalised and detained. There have been moments she has felt tempted to join them. But the thought of her mother and their uncertain housing situation have held her back.
“I am not scared any more. I have gone through the worst already,” she said. But she doesn’t want to put her mother through more pain.
Days before the protest, R had been planning her 15th birthday. She wanted to cut her birthday cake inside an autorickshaw, to remake a trend she had seen on social media.

It’s been a couple of months since she turned 15. I asked her what she wants or hopes for now. She paused and then said: “My past is not in my hands. I can’t change that. Now, I just want to look ahead and do well in my board exams.”
What else we’re reading about

blocks.caption: A still from award-winning film Selvi.

blocks.text: Culture | Two Indian films won awards at the Busan international film festival. Birds in the Dark by Shashank Walia was awarded the Songwon Vision audience prize and Sailesh Rathnakumar’s Selvi won the HyLife Vision as well as the Taipei Film Commission award.
